potential_divergence_points.description: API/MCP apply time_budget_hours as a skill-list truncation; direct engine call returns full list.
potential_divergence_points.impact: List LENGTH differs, but ORDERING of included skills is identical.
potential_divergence_points.handling: Consistency tests compare order-within-included-skills, not absolute count.

potential_divergence_points.description: BlueprintGenerator generates a timestamp-based ID on every call.
potential_divergence_points.impact: blueprint.id value differs between calls but content fields are identical.
potential_divergence_points.severity: Low — ID is excluded from parity checks.
potential_divergence_points.handling: Consistency test strips 'id' and 'generated_at' before comparison.

root_cause_analysis.description: All three layers (Engine, API /recommend, MCP recommend_skills) share a single execution path. API calls engine.recommend() then calibrator.calibrate_ids() directly. MCP calls the API TestClient which routes to the same handler. No business logic is duplicated; therefore structural parity is guaranteed by design.

final_scores.production_readiness_rationale: All three layers produce identical outputs. -3 points: time_budget_hours truncation is not surfaced in MCP layer documentation; blueprint timestamps make exact equality assertions fragile without field exclusion.
